expected_output.reasoning:
The response does a thorough job on several fronts: it enumerates guardrails, identifies that the strongest guardrail is DRAFT-only (correctly avoiding evaluating a DRAFT as if production-ready), discloses unverified areas (code path, unreviewed guardrails, other roles/compute, real traffic), and gives read-only remediation steps (create guardrail from demo, add grounding/PII checks, enforce via IAM condition, publish numbered version). It also avoids reproducing blocked prompt/completion text.

However, it fails on specific required elements:
1. It never raises or cites the specific check-id "LLM-GRD-001" at CRITICAL severity as required by the expected output. There is no structured check-id/severity scheme used anywhere in the response.
2. It does not cite any AWS-doc citation for findings — no links or references to AWS documentation are provided for any of the findings.
3. Critically, it prints the raw 12-digit AWS account ID: "What I verified (account 012345678901_1, us-east-1 and us-west-2)" — this directly violates the explicit requirement "It never prints a raw 12-digit account ID."

Given the explicit violation of printing the raw account ID, plus the complete absence of the LLM-GRD-001 check-id/severity framework and AWS-doc citations, the response does not meet the expected output criteria despite being substantively good in other areas.
